title: Japanese-Style Pork Gyudon
description: A popular Japanese dish featuring thinly sliced pork and onions in a savory broth, served over rice.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: Thinly slice the pork against the grain.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Springy onions add a great texture to the dish.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use Japanese soy sauce for an authentic flavor.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance out the savory flavors with a touch of sweetness.

ingredients.name: Rice vinegar
ingredients.notes: Add a hint of acidity to the dish.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Grate the ginger using a microplane for an even flavor.

ingredients.name: Zesty dashi broth
ingredients.notes: Dashi is a traditional Japanese broth made from dried seaweed and dried fish.

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.notes: Use springy green onions for garnish.

instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced pork and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove the pork from the skillet and set aside.
Add the sliced onions to the skillet and cook until they are softened and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, and rice vinegar to the skillet and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the dashi broth to the skillet and bring to a simmer.
Add the cooked pork back to the skillet and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the pork is coated in the sauce.
Serve the pork and onions over a bed of steaming hot rice.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and serve immediately.
